en: To do something kind or helpful for someone.
ex: Could you do me a favor and watch my bag?
你能幫我個忙看一下我的包嗎？

en: To complete something successfully; or to connect someone by telephone.
ex: Please put me through to the manager.
請幫我轉接給經理。

en: To deal successfully with a difficult situation or task.
ex: She is coping with the loss very well.
她很好地面對失去親人的痛苦。

en: To start to love someone or something.
ph: fall head over heels in love
col: fall in love at first sight
ex: He fell in love with her smile.
他愛上了她的笑容。

en: To go and do small jobs for someone, such as delivering messages or buying things.
ex: I have to run a few errands this afternoon.
我今天下午得辦幾件雜事。

en: To begin to like someone or something; or to begin doing something regularly.
ex: The kids quickly took to their new teacher.
孩子們很快就喜歡上新老師。

en: To do something you did not have time to do earlier; or to learn about recent events.
ex: I need to catch up on my homework.
我得趕緊補完作業。

en: To look at the things or people around you.
ex: He looked about for a place to sit.
他四處張望找位子坐。

en: To accept a job or responsibility; or to employ someone.
ex: She took on more responsibility at work.
她在工作上承擔了更多責任。

en: To be careful; or used as a way of saying goodbye.
ex: Take care when you cross the street.
過馬路時要小心。

en: To finish paying money that you owe; or to produce a good result after a lot of effort.
ex: It took him ten years to pay off his debts.
他花了十年還清債務。

en: To grasp something firmly; or to take control of something.
ex: He took hold of her hand and led her across.
他抓住她的手帶她過去。

en: To manage to obtain something; or to find someone and be able to contact them.
ex: I couldn't get hold of him by phone.
我打電話聯絡不上他。

en: To gradually lose power or energy; or to become less active or worse.
ex: The clock ran down because no one wound it.
時鐘因為沒人上發條而停了。

en: To earn or produce money; or to introduce something new.
ex: The shop brings in about a thousand dollars a day.
這家店一天約有一千元收入。

en: To fall to the ground; or to become lower; or to arrive from a higher place.
ex: Prices have come down since last year.
價格自去年以來已經下降。

en: To raise something to a higher position; or to build or fix something in place.
ex: They put up a tent by the lake.
他們在湖邊搭了一頂帳篷。

en: To cause something to fall by hitting it; or to stop work; or to reduce a price.
ex: The cat knocked the vase off the shelf.
貓把花瓶從架子上撞了下來。

en: To often or regularly do something, usually something annoying.
ex: Stop going around telling people what to do.
別再到處指使別人了。

en: To place something inside something else; or to add or include something.
ex: Put some salt in the soup.
在湯裡加點鹽。

en: To fall in a rough and uncontrolled way; or to collapse.
ex: The old wall tumbled down in the storm.
舊牆在暴風雨中倒塌了。

en: To remove something by blowing it away; or to impress someone very much.
ex: The wind blew away all the dead leaves.
風把所有枯葉都吹走了。

en: To stay behind and not move forward, because of fear or doubt.
ex: The shy boy hung back at the party.
那個害羞的男孩在派對上畏縮不前。

en: To take action to solve a problem; or to be about a particular subject.
ex: We have to deal with this problem immediately.
我們必須立刻處理這個問題。

en: To become ill with a common illness that causes a runny nose and cough.
ex: Wear a coat or you'll catch a cold.
穿件外套，不然你會感冒。

en: To choose someone or something from a group.
ex: She picked out a nice dress for the party.
她為派對挑了一件漂亮的洋裝。

en: To throw things carelessly in different directions.
ex: Don't throw your clothes around the room.
不要把衣服亂丟在房間裡。

en: To scold someone severely; or to ask for something from above.
ex: The teacher called him down for talking in class.
老師因他在課堂上說話而責備他。

en: To make a short visit to someone or somewhere.
col: look in on my way home
ex: I'll look in on you tomorrow.
我明天順道去看你。

en: To send a letter or message you have received to another person or address.
ex: Please send on this email to the team.
請把這封郵件轉給團隊。

en: To succeed in doing something difficult.
ex: She carried off the performance brilliantly.
她出色地完成了這場表演。

en: To spend time in a place doing nothing in particular.
ex: A group of kids were hanging around outside the shop.
一群孩子在店外閒晃。

en: To have a good opinion of someone or something.
ex: Everyone thinks well of our new neighbor.
大家都對新鄰居印象很好。

en: To bring something down from a higher place; or to feel sad.
ex: Can you get that book down from the top shelf?
你能把那本書從最上層拿下來嗎？

en: To pay part of the price immediately; or to reduce the amount of a debt.
ex: They paid down a third of the price on the car.
他們先付了三分之一的車款。

en: To consider something when making a judgment or decision.
ex: You must take the weather into account.
你必須把天氣因素考慮進去。

en: To pass without any serious results; or to be forgotten after a short time.
ex: Don't worry; this scandal will soon blow over.
別擔心，這件醜聞很快就會平息。

en: To reach a particular amount; or to run quickly upward.
ex: He ran up a huge bill at the restaurant.
他在餐廳累積了一大筆帳單。

en: To say something that you know is not true.
col: tell a lie to cover up
ex: You should never tell a lie to your parents.
你絕不該對父母說謊。

en: To leave a place; or to stop a habit; or to avoid doing something.
ex: She got out of doing the dishes by pretending to be sick.
她假裝生病而逃過洗碗。
